unit: Power: Monarchy and Democracy in Britain c.1000-2014
title: Tudor monarchy and Parliament

items.title: Lesson Podcast
items.description: Audio walkthrough of how Henry VIII used Parliament to break with Rome, and how Elizabeth I managed parliamentary relations.

items.title: Ten Minute English and British History #17 — The Early Tudors: Henry VIII and the Reformation
items.description: Clear overview of how Henry VIII co-opted Parliament to achieve the break with Rome — Parliament empowered and constrained.

items.title: When Did Britain's Kings Lose Their Power?
items.description: Traces the gradual shift of power from monarch to Parliament — the Tudor period as a critical turning point. 12 min.

items.title: Wolf Hall (2015)
items.description: Thomas Cromwell navigating Henry VIII's court — the relationship between royal will, Parliament and the Reformation.

items.title: The Tudors (2007)
items.description: Henry VIII's reign dramatised — how he used Parliament as a tool and what that did to the constitution.

items.title: A Man for All Seasons (1966)
items.description: Thomas More's refusal to accept Henry's supremacy — conscience, law and the limits of royal power over Parliament.

items.title: Parliament UK — Teaching Resources
items.description: Official Parliament UK resources on the Tudor Parliament and its relationship with the monarchy.
